$comment: G-SQL executable corpus, step 2. Each case runs against its own dialect backend only; cross-dialect feeding is prevented structurally by separate entry points plus a dedicated selection test (D03). params/row_limit follow the descriptor contract: total = len(params)+1 for row-returning shapes with the LIMIT site binding the trailing number, total = len(params) for execute. expect=valid means the full descriptor check accepts; expect.invalid names the required rejection category: syntax | multi_statement | bad_kind | bad_limit | returning | param_unknown | param_unused | param_name. Placeholders: postgresql $N; sqlite ? ?NNN :name @name $name; mysql ? positional. Assumed sql_mode for mysql cases is the server default (no ANSI_QUOTES); the qualified backend must document its mode.

cases.statement: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT $2
UPDATE users SET name = $1 WHERE id = $2

cases.notes: quoted semicolon and quoted $N-like text are literal, never statement or parameter sites
cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE nick = ';$9;' AND id = $1 LIMIT $2

cases.notes: line and block comments swallow $N-like text
cases.statement:
SELECT name FROM users -- $1 is not a param
WHERE id = $1 /* $2 neither */ LIMIT $2
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT $2; SELECT 1

cases.notes: RETURNING is never admitted even where the engine supports it
cases.statement: UPDATE users SET name = $1 WHERE id = $2 RETURNING id
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $1
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT 10
WITH u AS (SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = $1) SELECT id FROM u LIMIT $2
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $3 LIMIT $2
SELECT 1
DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1

cases.notes: baseline positional ? shape; sites map 1..M in order
cases.statement: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?
UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?

cases.notes: ?NNN out of order; LIMIT binds the trailing number
cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE a = ?2 AND b = ?1 LIMIT ?3

cases.notes: quoted semicolons, doubled-quote escape, double-quoted identifier, and $N-like text inside a literal are never sites
cases.statement: SELECT "na;me" FROM users WHERE nick = 'it''s; $1' AND id = ? LIMIT ?
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?; SELECT 1

cases.notes: SQLite supports RETURNING; Can still forbids it
cases.statement: UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ? RETURNING id
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT 10
WITH u AS (SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = ?) SELECT id FROM u LIMIT ?
SELECT name FROM users WHERE a = ?1 AND b = ?2 LIMIT ?4

cases.notes: line and block comments swallow ? text
cases.statement:
SELECT name FROM users -- ? not a param
WHERE id = ? /* ? neither */ LIMIT ?
SELECT "select" FROM "users" WHERE "id" = ? LIMIT ?

cases.notes: named spellings map onto numbers (:id is 1, :lim is the trailing 2); non-limit named sites must spell their declared parameter, the limit name is free
cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = :id LIMIT :lim
SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?
UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?
SELECT `select`, `id` FROM `users` WHERE `id` = ? LIMIT ?

cases.notes: backslash escape inside a string under default sql_mode; the escaped quote does not end the literal
cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE nick = 'a\'b' AND id = ? LIMIT ?
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?; SELECT 1

cases.notes: TiDB grammar admits the RETURNING shape (TiDB itself rejects it in planning, real MySQL in prepare); the backend exposes it structurally and Can rejects it as RETURNING, never admitted
cases.statement: UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ? RETURNING id
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?

cases.notes: two LIMIT sites cannot both bind the single trailing number
cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?, ?
WITH u AS (SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = ?) SELECT id FROM u LIMIT ?

cases.notes: three ? sites exceed the declared total of two
cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE a = ? AND b = ? LIMIT ?

cases.notes: hash, double-dash (with required space), and block comments swallow ? text

cases.statement: UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?
SELECT * FORM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT $2
cases.notes: grammar failure surfaces verbatim with cursor

cases.statement: SELECT * FORM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?
cases.notes: grammar failure, TiDB and MySQL agree

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?, ?
cases.notes: two LIMIT sites cannot bind the single trailing number

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
cases.notes: OFFSET form binds two sites; Can admits exactly one

cases.statement: SELECT * FORM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?
cases.notes: ERROR nodes with spans; LIMIT present so only syntax is wrong

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE nick = 'unterminated AND id = ? LIMIT ?
cases.notes: unterminated literal is ERROR to end of input

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ? LIMIT ?;
cases.notes: one trailing semicolon admitted and tiled as text

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT $3
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?1 LIMIT ?3
SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $1 LIMIT ?
cases.notes: digit-led $ names are rejected by the grammar, like the engine

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = :idd LIMIT :lim
cases.notes: misspelled site name is caught even though numbering works
